The return list reads request while its other operand json.Unmarshal mutates request through its address; separate unmarshaling from the return to avoid depending on operand evaluation order.
The generic file-request decoder returns request in the same operand list as json.Unmarshal writes through &request, creating an evaluation-order-dependent returned value.
The recall decoder returns request alongside the Unmarshal call that mutates it, rather than unmarshaling before computing the returned value.
The skill decoder reads request and mutates it through &request in one return operand list; this relies on unspecified relative evaluation of the variable read and call.

The long-running-command helper registers SIGINT cleanup and relies on CommandContext cancellation to kill if needed, but never calls Wait; signals and cancellation do not reap the child or finish output-copy workers.

The Eventually callback polls until TLS certificates are removed and discards any interim successful response. The fake server writes hello-world, so successful responses before asynchronous certificate removal require closure even though the final expected result is a handshake failure.

The handler writes no body, but phttp.Default sets a three-hour Client timeout and wraps Transport; net/http wraps even an empty response in cancelTimerBody, whose timer cancellation requires EOF or Close. Discarding the response retains that cancellation resource until timeout.
cacheWriterHelper closes its opened file only at the final success return; Write or Sync errors return first without deferred cleanup. The lock defer releases only v.lock, not the file.
Legacy Bolt Open closes db on flock failure, but subsequent file.Stat or db.init errors return directly without closing the acquired db.file or releasing its lock.
Test starts a helper process and only kills it at the end, with earlier Fatal paths also skipping that kill. No Wait reaps the child; attaching Cmd for pause/resume does not schedule cleanup.

nextEnd deliberately retains nextMutex on terminal stream/error elements; its caller Close already marks shutdown and then closes the connection. Repeated Close or readers already past shutdown can still block, so correctness depends on the shutdown/concurrency contract; not classified as either a proven bug or harmless FP.

Run starts TinyDNS before SOCKS setup; SplitHostPort, ParseUint, or NewSuperProxy errors return before the final wg.Wait and without stopping or joining that DNS worker.

TinyDNS.New acquires hybrid-map storage; later dialer, proxy transport, or mux setup errors return without tdns.Close before ownership reaches the returned Proxy.
